extension_description.message: Privacy-first browser sync to your own storage: Google Drive, WebDAV, GitHub.
extension_description.description: Shown in the browser's extension list, and used as the store summary when the listing does not override it.

datatype_bookmarks.description: One of the four data types. Also a section heading in Settings.

datatype_history.description: One of the four data types.

datatype_sessions.description: One of the four data types: the tabs a device has open.

datatype_extensions.description: One of the four data types: the list of installed extensions.

status_idle.description: Sync status: nothing is happening and nothing is wrong. Not 'finished'. This is the resting state.

status_syncing.description: Sync status: a sync is running now.

status_success.description: Sync status: the last sync completed.

status_error.description: Sync status: the last sync failed.

status_conflict.description: Sync status: a conflict is waiting for the user to choose a version.

stream_off.description: Per-data-type state, shown in a tooltip after the type name: this type is turned off in Settings. Lower case: it follows 'Bookmarks: '.

stream_syncing.description: Per-data-type state: this type is being synced right now.

stream_pending.description: Per-data-type state: a sync is running but has not reached this type yet.

stream_never.description: Per-data-type state: this type has never completed a sync. Must not sound like success.

stream_stale.description: Per-data-type state: this type has synced before, but the most recent attempt failed.

stream_synced.description: Per-data-type state: this type synced successfully.

popup_settings_aria.description: Accessible name of the gear button in the popup's top-right corner.

popup_sync_now.description: The popup's primary button. While a sync runs it shows status_syncing instead.

popup_load_error.message: Couldn't reach Konode. Tap to retry.
popup_load_error.description: The popup could not read its own state. The whole banner is a button, hence 'tap to retry'.

popup_recovery_notice.message: An unusual deletion ($COUNT$ bookmarks) was blocked and a restore point was saved. Review in Settings → Activity.
popup_recovery_notice.description: The mass-delete guard refused a peer's deletions. Reassuring by design: nothing was lost. 'Settings → Activity' names a tab, so it must match the tab's own translation.

popup_no_backend.description: No storage provider has been set up yet. The banner opens Settings.

popup_conflict_title.description: A conflict is waiting for a decision. $TYPE$ is a data type name (bookmarks, history, sessions, extensions).

popup_keep_local.description: Conflict resolution: keep what this device has.

popup_use_remote.description: Conflict resolution: take the other device's version.

popup_active_streams.description: Heading above the four data-type dots. The stylesheet displays it in capitals, so do not capitalise it here.

popup_missing_extensions_one.description: Exactly one extension is installed on another device but not on this one.

popup_missing_extensions_other.description: More than one extension is installed on another device but not on this one. In languages that use the singular after a numeral, this is the same wording as the _one form.

popup_open_all.description: Opens a store page for every missing extension, one tab each.

popup_sessions_head.description: Heading above the restorable sessions list. The stylesheet displays it in capitals, so do not capitalise it here.

popup_unknown_device.description: Fallback name for a peer device whose session carries no label.

popup_tabs_one.description: How many tabs a peer's session holds, in the case of exactly one.

popup_tabs_other.description: How many tabs a peer's session holds. In languages that use the singular after a numeral, this is the same wording as the _one form.

popup_restore.description: Opens the tabs of a peer device's session. Adds tabs; removes nothing.

popup_backend_label.description: Footer label before the storage provider's name.

popup_backend_none.description: Footer value when no storage provider is set up.

popup_device_label.description: Footer label before this device's name.

popup_configure.description: Footer link to Settings. Keep the arrow.

popup_activity_log.description: Footer link that opens Settings on the Activity tab. Keep the arrow.

common_show.description: Tooltip on the eye button that reveals a password.

common_hide.description: Tooltip on the eye button that hides a password again.

provider_gdrive_desc.message: Syncs straight to your own Google Drive. Thanks to OAuth, the access token is kept on this device only.

provider_nextcloud_desc.message: Your own Nextcloud or ownCloud server.

provider_nextcloud_note.message: Enter just your server host; use an App Password (Settings → Security).
provider_nextcloud_note.description: Extra hint shown under the card once it is selected.

provider_pcloud_desc.message: pCloud storage. Needs a paid pCloud plan.

provider_pcloud_note.message: Pick the $REGION$ region if that is where your pCloud account lives.

provider_koofr_note.message: Use your Koofr email as the username, and a Koofr app password as the password.

provider_fastmail_note.message: Use your full Fastmail address as the username, and an app password that has Files (WebDAV) access.

provider_github_desc.message: Your synced data lives in a private GitHub repository, which Konode reaches with a Personal Access Token.

provider_webdav_desc.message: Synology, kDrive, or any other WebDAV server.

provider_syncing_to.description: $URL$ is rendered in a monospace <code> element, so the sentence is split at the placeholder rather than interpolated. Keep the placeholder as one piece.

onb_welcome_subtitle.message: Browser sync where your data stays genuinely yours. Your bookmarks, sessions and extensions go straight to storage you own. No server in between.

onb_feature_storage.message: Your data always stays on storage you own.

onb_feature_instant.message: Syncs every change as it happens.

onb_feature_browsers.message: Works in Chromium and Firefox based browsers.

onb_feature_providers.message: You decide where your data lives.

onb_backend_subtitle.message: Where should Konode store your data?

onb_use_provider.description: Accessible name of a storage-provider card. $PROVIDER$ is a brand name and is never translated.

onb_drive_unavailable.message: Google sign-in isn't available in this browser. Pick another option.

onb_signin_failed.description: Last-resort text when the sign-in threw something with no message of its own.

onb_github_401.message: GitHub rejected this token. Check it hasn't expired, and that you pasted all of it.

onb_github_unreachable.message: Couldn't reach GitHub. Check your connection and try again.

onb_github_token_link.message: Create a fine-grained token (only this repo) →

onb_data_subtitle.message: You can change this anytime in Settings.

onb_device_name_desc.message: How it appears in the session list on your other devices.

onb_device_name_placeholder.description: An example name, not a default. The field arrives pre-filled with the detected one.

onb_encrypt_subtitle.message: If you turn encryption on, your data is encrypted on this device before it is uploaded. Not even your storage provider can read what it contains.

onb_pass_placeholder.message: Choose a passphrase, or generate an encryption key

onb_pass_missing.message: Enter a passphrase, or generate a key.

onb_pass_too_short.message: At least $MIN$ characters. Synced data can be attacked offline, so short passphrases are guessable.

onb_save_passphrase_lead.description: Shown in bold, immediately before onb_save_passphrase_rest. One sentence on its own.

onb_save_passphrase_rest.message: It never leaves this device and cannot be recovered if you lose it. You have to enter the same passphrase on every device. You can copy it later in Settings.

onb_plaintext_note.message: Without encryption, your data goes to your own storage $WORD$. That can be the right choice if you fully trust your storage provider. You can turn encryption on later in Settings at any time.
onb_plaintext_note.description: $WORD$ is onb_plaintext_word, shown in bold inside this sentence, so the sentence is split at the placeholder.

onb_plaintext_word.description: The bold word dropped into onb_plaintext_note. Lower case: it sits mid-sentence.

onb_err_bad_webdav_url.message: That WebDAV address doesn't look like a valid URL.

onb_err_perms_webdav.message: Konode needs permission to reach your WebDAV server and the data types you chose. Please allow them to continue.

onb_err_perms_types.message: Some permissions were declined. Grant them, or turn off those data types, to continue.

onb_err_read_settings.message: Couldn't read your current settings. Try again.

onb_err_save.description: $ERROR$ is a message from the engine and stays in English. See CLAUDE.md on why the diagnostic layer is not translated.

onb_sync_subtitle.message: Konode is running its first sync. This also runs in the background, so you don't have to wait here.

onb_sync_error_subtitle.message: Your settings are saved. Open Settings to fix this, or finish and let Konode retry in the background.

onb_sync_timeout.message: This is taking longer than usual. A large history can do that. The sync keeps running in the background, so you can finish now.

onb_done_subtitle.message: Konode is now syncing your browser data to $BACKEND$. The first sync is already running in the background.
onb_done_subtitle.description: $BACKEND$ is shown in bold and is a brand name, so the sentence is split at the placeholder.

onb_done_autosync.message: Syncing runs automatically in the background

onb_done_adjust.message: You can change the settings at any time

datatype_bookmarks_desc.message: Full bookmark tree with folders and ordering.
datatype_bookmarks_desc.description: Shown under the data type on BOTH the setup wizard and Settings. The two screens used to carry different wording and drifted apart.

datatype_sessions_desc.message: Named tab sessions you can restore anywhere.
datatype_sessions_desc.description: Deliberately not 'tab groups': that names a Chrome feature Konode does not sync, which the setup wizard used to claim.

datatype_history_desc.message: Browsing history, limited by the days setting.
datatype_history_desc.description: Not a fixed number of days: the setup wizard used to promise 'Last 30 days' while the limit is adjustable in Settings.

datatype_extensions_desc.message: Extension list, showing missing ones with install links.
